review.overall_assessment:
Status: the m2p_crawler_dozer model, lesson and META are about 75% ready for trainee use. The class sizing is right: ~70 t, ~450 kW, 2.55 m gauge, 610 mm shoes, a semi-U blade about 4.9 m wide and 2.1 m high holding ~18.5 m³, oval track with 8 rollers, double-reduction final drives, and parallelogram single-shank ripper. The blade mouldboard, wing angles, end-bit positions and the push-arm trunnion pivot are well done, and most of the text is correct. The quiz answers are correct and unambiguous apart from Q4's slot-dozing wording.

Major issues to fix before release:
(1) The push arms pass through the track chain; they must move outboard to y ≈ ±1.75 m.
(2) The ripper's upper parallelogram link is rotated about the lower pin, so the linkage visibly comes apart in the animation.
(3) The machine never travels, so the ripper is shown plunging about 1.2 m into ground at standstill, which is the wrong technique.
(4) The cab is about 0.5 m too high (ROPS top 4.7 m vs the 4.0–4.2 m design basis), which also exposes floating drivetrain boxes.
(5) The operation tab is missing 'never turn or reverse with the ripper in the ground'.
(6) The safety and start-up text is missing the attachments-down/LOTO, horn/area-clear and clearing hazards.
(7) Ripper depth is inconsistent with the design basis.

Minor items: fleet quantity (3+1), a reversed and mislabelled flow arrow (pump template text), shut-down order and interlocks, maintenance intervals, steering type for this class, oval vs elevated sprocket against the basis, raised ripper clearance, and missing ladder/GNSS details.

Confidence: high on the geometry and animation findings (checked against the code coordinates); medium on class figures such as penetration depth, raised clearance and ground pressure, since web verification was not available.

findings.where: _eq_m2p_mine.py L872-874 (discharge conveyor p0/p1) vs sizer_housing L842-853, sizer shafts L856, sizer_drives L859-870
findings.issue: The sacrificial conveyor starts at belt-top z of about 1.06 m at x=7.6 and climbs at 12 deg straight under and through the sizer and its drives. At x=9.6 the belt reaches the sizer base plate (z 1.2-1.5), and the discharge chute box (z 0.45-1.25) sits below the belt surface. By x=11.4 the belt centre (z of about 1.9) enters the tooth envelope, whose tips reach down to z 1.88. At x=14 the belt (centre z of about 2.4, edges y +/-0.7) runs through both right-angle gearboxes (z 1.95-3.25, |y| 0.1-1.0) and the gear couplings. This layout could not physically discharge product, and it teaches a trainee the wrong arrangement.
findings.correction: Run the sacrificial conveyor horizontally under the sizer in a trench or tunnel, then incline it once it is clear of the drive bases. Put the tail pulley centre at (SX0-2.0=6.6, 0, -1.25) so the belt top is at about -0.93 m. Keep it horizontal to x of about 17 m, which takes it past the drive bases at x 14 +/- 0.7 with at least 2 m of headroom for a walkway. Fit impact beds over x 7.6-14.0 (impact_len about 8 m). Then add a concave transition to 12 deg up to the A02 transfer. Extend the sizer discharge chute from the sizer base (z 1.2) down to a skirtboard about 0.5 m above the belt (z of about -0.4), keeping at least 0.6 m of clear height above the burden. Shift the magnet and metal-detector stations along the new path. If a trench is not wanted, raise the whole station instead: ZD, ZF and SZ each +2.5 m, with the conveyor tail at z of about 0.6 and horizontal under the sizer and drives.

findings.where: _eq_m2p_mine.py L770-771 (endw loop: x=HX0-0.5 width 1.0; x=HX1+1.5 width 3.0, z 1.0-10.0)
findings.issue: Both solid concrete end walls run from z=1.0 to z=10 across the full pocket width (|y| <= 4.7), and both of them swallow equipment. The head wall (x 6.0-9.0) encloses the feeder head sprocket (x 8, z 3.35), the head pans (to x 8.95), both shaft-mounted gearboxes and motors, the feeder walkway end, and the feed end of the sizer (bearings at x 8.0, end plate at 8.3). The tail wall (x -7.0 to -6.0) encloses the tail sprocket and pans (to x -7.96). The cutaway render shows the feeder running into solid concrete.
findings.correction: Head end: replace the 3 m block with a headwall or lintel over the feeder outlet, at x 6.0-7.0 and z from ZF+2.0 (5.9) to ZD. That leaves a discharge opening at least 2 m high for bed depth plus top lump. Leave x 7.0-16 open as the sizer and drive bay under a steel platform. Tail end: wall at x -7.0 to -6.0 with z from ZF+0.15 (4.05) to ZD, so it seals just above the pans. Alternatively move the wall behind the take-ups to x <= -8.3 if it is kept down to z=1.0.

findings.where: _sizer_shafts L725-741; call L856 (centres y=+/-0.55, R_hub 0.38, rings R 0.41, R_tip 0.72, ring x identical for j=0 and j=1)
findings.issue: The tooth-tip circles (dia 1.44 m) of the two shafts overlap by 0.34 m in the same axial planes, because both shafts put their rings at the same x positions. Each tip also reaches 0.03 m into the opposite shaft's ring collars (1.10 - 0.72 = 0.38 < 0.41). Each shaft has its own fluid-coupled drive, which slips on overload, so the shafts cannot be phase-timed and the teeth would clash. The closeup render shows this interpenetration.
findings.correction: Stagger shaft B's tooth rings by half the ring pitch, so each tooth on one shaft runs between two rings on the other. In _sizer_shafts use x = x0 + (x1-x0)*(r + 0.5 + 0.5*j)/rings, with rings-1 rings on shaft B, or shorten the last ring. Reduce R_tip to 0.66 m so the tips clear the opposite hub barrel by about 60 mm. Alternatively increase the shaft centres to 1.3 m (the top of the 1.0-1.3 m class) with R_tip 0.72 and R_hub/rings 0.45-0.48. Add a central breaker bar under and between the shafts (box 4.0 x 0.3 x 0.35 m at y=0, z=SZ-0.8) with slots for the teeth. This is the third breaking stage and the main top-size control in this sizer class.

findings.where: _eq_m2p_mine.py L902-905 (for p_, sgn in ((psa, 1), (psb, -1)))
findings.issue: Shaft A at y=-0.55 rotates +X, so its top moves toward -y. Shaft B at y=+0.55 rotates -X, so its top moves toward +y. Both tops therefore move OUTWARD, away from the centre. That is the reverse or jam-clearing direction. In normal sizing the shafts rotate inward at the top to draw lumps into the nip, as the lesson and basis both say.
findings.correction: Swap the signs to ((psa, -1), (psb, +1)), giving 12 rev / 10 s, about 72 rpm inward. Optionally add a short 'Reverse (jam clear)' clip with the signs inverted, to illustrate the auto-reverse interlock.

findings.issue: The feeder skirts and the hopper outlet (about 3.0 m clear) are WIDER than the 2.4 m pans, so ore would spill over the pan edges and onto the chains and rollers. On a real apron feeder the skirts sit inside the pan side flights, and the skirt opening (plus a margin) sets the bed width. Separately, 2.4 m pans are marginal for 1.2-1.5 m ROM top size: the rule of thumb is a skirt opening of at least about 2 x top lump.
findings.correction: Option A (keep the basis 2.4 m pans): skirts at y=+/-1.05 (2.1 m clear, diverging about 50 mm per metre toward the head), hopper outlet bottom at +/-1.0 to +/-1.05, and ROM top size in the lesson limited to about 1.0-1.2 m with oversize broken by the rock breaker. Option B (preferred for 1.5 m lumps): PW=3.0 m with skirts at +/-1.3 (2.6 m clear), feeder drives about 2 x 132-160 kW, and the sizer box widened to match. In both options add impact rails or rollers under the hopper section.

findings.where: content params.design_throughput, key_points[0]; META model_configuration.basis; ps_feeder/ps_conveyor 'capacity up to ~2,400 t/h'
findings.issue: The lesson states the design throughput as about 2,000-2,500 t/h. In the reference-plant basis, stream 'Sized ore to overland' is Design 1,800 t/h (nominal 1,300-1,500 t/h while crushing, about 4,300-4,900 h/yr), and 2,000-2,400 t/h is only the peak tipping rate and the equipment rating margin. As written, trainees would set the feeder 30-40 % above the 1,200 mm overland's design capacity.
findings.correction: Change design_throughput to P('≈ 1,300 – 1,500 nominal; 1,800 design', 't/h', 'Reference-plant basis (sized ore to overland, A01 stream 4)'). Add a parameter: sizer_feeder_rating = P('≈ 2,000 – 2,400', 't/h', 'Equipment rating margin for truck surges'). Change key_points[0] to 'Nominal ~1,300–1,500 t/h, design 1,800 t/h to the overland; feeder and sizer rated ~2,000–2,400 t/h for truck surges'. Change the META basis string to match.

findings.where: content params.tipping_deck_height ('≈ 8 – 10 m, Above the feeder') vs model ZD=10, ZF=3.9
findings.issue: The model puts the tipping deck 10 m above grade but only 6.1 m above the feeder pans (5.5 m above the hopper outlet), while the parameter says 8-10 m above the feeder. The 6 m hopper is consistent with the stated 200-300 t live capacity (about 316 m³ gross at 1.45 t/m³), so the parameter text is what needs to change.
findings.correction: Change it to P('≈ 10 above grade (≈ 6 above the feeder pans)', 'm', 'Model / engineering estimate'). Update the basis key_dimensions[1] to the same wording, or raise ZD to 12-14 m if 8-10 m above the feeder is kept.

findings.where: civil decks L757-759 (deck 16 m (x) x 14 m (y), ramp entering along x)
findings.issue: Each tipping deck is only 16 x 14 m. A 90 t-class rigid truck is about 10 m long with a turning-clearance circle of about 25 m. It arrives along +x and has to turn to face away from the hopper before reversing to the bund, which is impossible on this pad. Trainees would get a wrong idea of the space a dump station needs.
findings.correction: Make each deck at least about 32 m long (x) by 28 m deep (y): deck boxes (32.0, 28.0, 0.6) centred at y = s*(HW+0.4+14). Alternatively keep the size, add 'shown cut short' to the civil part name, and add a sentence to ps_civil: 'Each tipping pad must allow a full reverse manoeuvre: ≈ truck turning circle + truck length (≈ 30–35 m) clear.'

findings.where: rock_breaker L794-804 (pedestal at x=7.4, y=6.5 on the +y tipping deck); operation.alarms_interlocks
findings.issue: The breaker pedestal, power pack and cabin stand on the tipping deck, 1.2 m past the end of the wheel stop and right next to the truck reversing path, with no barrier. Its reach of about 7.4 m from that corner only covers the near half of the 12 x 8.6 m hopper; the far corner is about 17 m away. The lesson also never states the key interlock: no tipping while the breaker is working.
findings.correction: Move the pedestal off the tipping decks onto the head-end wall, centred over the feeder outlet where hang-ups and oversize collect: RBc = (HX1+1.5, 0, ZD), with the cabin on the +x side. Keep reach at 10-12 m, or add a second unit. If a corner position is kept per the basis, put it at x >= 9 behind a concrete barrier at least half the tyre height. Add to alarms_interlocks: 'Rock breaker in hopper (boom out of park) → both tipping lights red'. Add to safety: 'No tipping while the breaker is working; breaker exclusion zone for fragments'.

findings.where: content operation.alarms_interlocks, start_up, shut_down
findings.issue: The interlock list leaves out the sequence cascade that protects the plant. A downstream stop must stop the upstream equipment. Feeder zero-speed, sizer underspeed and bearing temperature, chute-blocked, and belt-rip trips are also missing. The shut-down text ('run the feeder down to a safe level') conflicts with the tip 'never let the hopper run empty' and gives no run-out times.
findings.correction: alarms_interlocks: 'A02 overland stop → 01-CV-001 stop → sizer stop → feeder stop (sequence interlock)'; 'Sizer stall/overload → feeder stop, auto-reverse (2–3 attempts) then trip and alarm'; 'Zero-speed switches on feeder tail shaft and sizer shafts; sizer bearing temperature/vibration'; 'Blocked-chute probes at sizer discharge and head chute; belt rip detector; metal detector → belt stop + marker spray'; 'Rock breaker active / hopper high level → tipping lights red; hopper low level → alarm and slow the feeder to keep a protective layer'. start_up: 'Confirm A02 overland running (permissive), dust sprays on → magnet energised, metal detector healthy → discharge conveyor → sizer (inward) → feeder at minimum speed; then green lights'. shut_down: 'Red lights; leave ≥ ~1 truck load in the hopper to protect the pans (empty it only for liner/pan work); stop feeder → sizer runs empty ~30–60 s → stop sizer → belt runs empty → stop conveyor → de-energise magnet; isolate'.

findings.where: content curve; principle step 4; META ps_shafts
findings.issue: The curve text says product top size rises with shaft speed. In this sizer class, top size is set mainly by the tooth and ring spacing and the shaft-to-breaker-bar gap, and it grows as the teeth wear. Speed mainly changes capacity. The breaker-bar stage of breakage is also missing from the explanation.
findings.correction: curve: 'Sizer capacity rises with shaft speed and shaft length; product top size is set by tooth/ring spacing and the gap to the breaker bar and grows as teeth wear; feeder speed is controlled to keep the sizer evenly loaded within motor power and the overland design rate.' Append to step 4: '…lumps that pass the first nip are snapped against the breaker bar beneath the shafts (third stage).'

findings.where: content quiz Q7 option 0
findings.issue: The answer cites a '1,200–1,400 mm overland belt', but the basis sets the overland at 1,200 mm (the 1,400 mm belt is the sacrificial conveyor). The lump-size reasoning is also left vague.
findings.correction: Option 0: 'It suits the 1,200 mm overland belt and its transfer chutes (lump ≤ about 1/5–1/6 of belt width with fines)'. Explanation: 'CEMA lump-size guidance and chute clearances limit top size; the refinery does its own secondary crushing and grinding.'

findings.where: ore lumps L917-939 (r 0.3/0.42, product scale 0.38); pan animation L900-901
findings.issue: Product lumps on the belt are drawn 0.23-0.32 m across, which contradicts the '-200 mm' label. ROM lumps are only 0.6-0.84 m, under the 1.2-1.5 m top size. The feeder pans are animated as one rigid block shifting +x, so the return strand also appears to move toward the sizer.
findings.correction: Set the ROM lump radius to 0.35/0.6 (0.7-1.2 m) and the product scale to 0.15 (about 0.11-0.18 m). Animate each pan along MK.track_point(sx + v*t) so the carry run moves +x and the return run moves -x, at 0.12-0.15 m/s for the 1,800 t/h design rate.

findings.where: META ps_tramp; tramp_metal L886-890; content principle step 6
findings.issue: The metal detector is only about 14 m from the head pulley (at 34 m of 48 m). At 2.5-3 m/s that leaves about 5 s to stop the belt before the metal reaches the transfer. The notes also do not say why the detector is essential here: broken apron-feeder pans and hammer pieces made of manganese steel are non-magnetic, so the magnet cannot catch them.
findings.correction: Place the detector so its distance to the head pulley is at least belt speed x coast-down time plus 5 m (for example magnet at 14 m, detector at 22 m, giving at least 26 m to the head). Add to ps_tramp: 'Austenitic manganese steel (feeder pans, liners, hammer tools) is non-magnetic — only the metal detector catches it.' Add the belt rip detector and belt scale (basis items) to ps_conveyor.

findings.where: hopper spray ring L789-791; deck edges at x -8 to -7 and 7 to 8 beside the pocket
findings.issue: The 14 dust-spray nozzles lie on an ellipse inscribed in the hopper opening, so most of them float in mid-air over the hopper. Around x -8 to -7 the deck edge drops about 10 m into the feeder pocket with no handrail or barrier, while the basis calls for handrails at all edges.
findings.correction: Place the nozzles on a header along the rock-box ledges at y=+/-(HW-0.3), z=ZD+0.2 (5 per side) and on the end walls (2 per end), angled down and inward. Add handrails (1.1 m) along y=+/-(HW+0.4) wherever the deck edge is not protected by the wheel-stop bund.

findings.where: META standards[2] 'MDG 15 / site rules'
findings.issue: MDG 15 is the NSW guideline for mobile and transportable equipment. It does not set dump bund or wheel-stop heights.
findings.correction: Replace it with {'code': 'Site dump-design standard / regulator guidance (e.g. WA & QLD mine dump and windrow guidance)', 'title': 'Dump-point wheel stops and windrows ≥ ½ the largest tyre diameter', 'relevance': 'Wheel stops'}.

findings.where: sizer_housing L842-850; feeder head L812 vs sizer end plate x=8.3
findings.issue: The sizer housing is open-topped, but the basis and safety notes rely on closed top covers against ejected fragments and on a dust hood. The feeder head pans (to x 8.95, z 2.8-3.9) also overlap the sizer feed-end plate at x 8.3.
findings.correction: Add removable top covers over x SX0+1.0 to SX1 (leaving a feed opening of about 1.2 m under the feeder head) and a dust-extraction hood at the discharge. Move the sizer to SX0 = FX1+1.4 (9.4 m) with a short head chute, or drop the end plate to z <= 2.6 under the head.

review.overall_assessment:
Current status: the lesson content for this model is mostly right for its class, but the 3-D layout has several physical impossibilities, so it is not ready for trainees as built. The lesson correctly covers why a twin-shaft sizer suits sticky lateritic bauxite, the apron feeder role, wheel stops at least half the tyre height, fluid couplings, the magnet-then-detector order, the confined-space and engulfment rules, and the start-up order. Parts present and naming are right for the class.

The geometry has four serious problems:
- The sacrificial conveyor climbs through the sizer base, the tooth envelope and both drive gearboxes.
- Both concrete end walls enclose the feeder head and tail and the sizer feed end.
- The two shafts' tooth envelopes overlap in the same planes even though each shaft has its own slipping drive.
- The shafts are animated turning outward, which is the reverse/jam-clear direction, not normal sizing.

There are also skirt and outlet widths larger than the pans, tipping decks too small for a 90 t truck to manoeuvre, and a rock breaker placed in the truck path. On the content side, the design throughput (2,000–2,500 t/h) conflicts with the basis value of 1,800 t/h design (1,300–1,500 nominal) to the 1,200 mm overland, the deck height above the feeder disagrees with the model, and the interlock and shut-down texts lack the sequence cascade and the "no tipping while the breaker works" rule. Maintenance intervals, failure modes and the quiz are sound apart from the overland belt width in Q7.

Confidence: high on the geometry clashes and the throughput inconsistency (both computed from the code and the basis), medium on the class details (tooth staggering and breaker bar, deck size, apron-feeder width rule).

findings.where: content/m2p_mine.py MODULES['m2p_blasthole_drill'].safety; operation.normal; quiz
findings.issue: The safety list leaves out the top drill-and-blast hazard: drilling into or next to old sockets/butts or misfired holes, and drilling near charged holes. The basis lists it ('never drill into or near old sockets'). The list also leaves out the 8.6 m mast near overhead power lines, the noise and silica hazards outside the cab, and the stored energy in the compressed air and hydraulic accumulators. As written, a trainee sees three generic bullets and none of the hazards that kill drillers.
findings.correction: Replace safety with: ['Never drill into or within the site minimum distance of an old socket/butt, a bootleg or a misfired hole; inspect and mark the pattern before drilling and report any suspected explosive residue to the shotfirer.', 'Never drill in a pattern once charging has started, except under the site procedure and at the site minimum distance from charged holes.', 'Check overhead clearance before raising or tramming with the feed up: the ~9 m mast must keep the site minimum approach distance to power lines.', 'Position the rig at right angles to the crest and outside the edge-hazard zone (site rule) when drilling the front row; tram with the feed in the tramming position, within OEM slope/tilt limits.', 'Rotating rods and rod handling: exclusion zone around the feed while drilling, guards and rod-handling interlocks, never reach into the feed.', 'Respirable crystalline silica and noise (top hammer > 100 dB(A) at the rig): dust collector working, closed pressurised cab, RPE and hearing protection outside the cab.', 'Before maintenance: isolate, blow down the compressor and air lines (whip checks on hoses), and depressurise the hydraulics and rock-drill accumulators (LOTO).', 'After charging: blast exclusion zone (typically ≥ 300–500 m for people, site-specific) and misfire procedures.']. Add to operation.normal at the front: 'Check the collar for old sockets/misfire indications before collaring'. Add a quiz question: 'You find an old socket near a pegged hole. What do you do?' → 'Do not drill; mark it and report to the shotfirer/supervisor' (distractors: 'Drill through it quickly', 'Flush it with air', 'Move the peg 0.5 m and drill').

findings.where: content params.pattern_burden_x_spacing ('≈ 3.5–4.5 × 3.5–4.5'); key_points[0] ('~4 × 4 m'); META summary and dr_pattern ('~3.5–4.5 m (here 4 × 4 m)'); builder blast_pattern (i*4.0, -8+j*4.0); part name
findings.issue: The pattern conflicts with the basis (B × S 2.5–3.5 × 3.0–4.0 m, nominal 3.0 × 3.5 m) and is also poor blasting practice for shallow benches. With a 102 mm hole, ~3.5 m deep, ~2 m stemming and ~1.5 m of emulsion at ~8 kg/m (≈12 kg), a 4 × 4 × 3 m block of 48 m³ gives about 0.25 kg/m³, below the basis powder factor of 0.3–0.6 kg/m³. In a 1–4 m bench the stiffness ratio H/B is also well below 1 at B = 4 m, which leads to boulders, a hard toe and cratering/flyrock. On 3.0 × 3.5 m the same charge gives about 0.38 kg/m³, consistent with the basis.
findings.correction: Content: pattern_burden_x_spacing → P('≈ 2.5 – 3.5 × 3.0 – 4.0 (nominal 3.0 × 3.5)', 'm', 'Reference-plant design basis — engineering estimate; burden shrinks for thin caprock'). Add 'powder_factor': P('≈ 0.3 – 0.6', 'kg/m³ bank', 'Reference-plant design basis'). key_points[0] → 'Holes 89–127 mm on a ~3.0 × 3.5 m pattern (burden × spacing) in caprock 0.5–3 m thick; where the caprock is thinner than ~1–1.5 m, rip it with a dozer instead'. META summary → '~3.0 × 3.5 m pattern'. dr_pattern → 'Burden × spacing ~2.5–3.5 × 3.0–4.0 m (here 3.0 × 3.5 m) …'. Builder: x = PIV.x + i*3.0, y = -7.0 + j*3.5; bench box (14.0, 17.0, …) centred at (PIV.x + 4.0, 0, …). Part name → 'Drill pattern ~3.0 × 3.5 m (burden × spacing) …'.

findings.where: _eq_m2p_mine.py m2p_blasthole_drill: m.flow('air', [(-1.6,0.6,2.2),(2.5,0.6,1.8),(3.0,0,0.3)]); META overlay description
findings.issue: The flushing-air path runs from the compressor straight to a point on the ground 0.4 m from the collar. This teaches the wrong air route. Real flushing air goes from the compressor through a hose to the flushing head on the rock drill, down the bore of the rods, out of the bit flushing holes, and back up the annulus carrying the cuttings to the collar hood. From there it is sucked into the dust collector. The overlay description also still uses the pump template text 'Suction and discharge flow paths'.
findings.correction: Use two paths. 'air' (supply): (-1.6,0.6,2.2) → (2.3,0.3,2.0) → (2.6,0.3,6.0) → (2.6,0,5.5) [flushing head at mid-stroke] → (2.6,0,-2.5) [bit]. 'cuttings' (return, kind 'dust'): (2.6,0,-2.5) → (2.6,0,0.2) [collar hood] → (1.5,-0.7,1.0) → (-0.1,-0.7,2.0) [dust collector inlet]. If the rod/bit are moved forward of the beam (see geometry finding), change x 2.6 to 2.95. Overlay description → 'Flushing air down the rods and cuttings/dust return to the collector'. Principle step 4 → 'Flushing air from the screw compressor passes through the rock drill and down the hollow rods, leaves at the bit face and carries the cuttings up the annulus to the collar hood; the dust collector sucks off and filters the fines.'

findings.where: builder: feed pivot PIV=(2.6,0,1.6) directly on the frame front; no boom part; META dr_feed / code comment 'feed (mast) on a boom'
findings.issue: The model has no boom or feed cradle. The feed pivots on the front edge of the frame, so (a) the vertical beam (x 2.44–2.76) passes through the frame front (x ≤ 2.6, z 0.95–1.35); (b) the collar sits only ~0.45 m ahead of the track front (2.14), whereas in this class a hydraulic boom (lift/swing/feed dump/tilt) puts the collar ~1.5–2.5 m ahead and gives the coverage area for drilling several holes without tramming; (c) the comment and META describe a boom that is not modelled. The class also uses feed extension, where the feed slides in its cradle to put the foot on the ground, rather than the beam hanging 1.5 m below the pivot.
findings.correction: Add part 'boom' (ref 'dr_boom', META: 'Hydraulic boom with lift, swing and feed-dump/tilt cylinders; sets hole position and angle within the coverage area'): a box 2.0 × 0.35 × 0.35 m from a boom foot at (2.2,0,1.5) to a cradle at (3.9,0,2.0), plus a lift cylinder (r 0.07) from (1.6,0,1.1) to (3.0,0,1.85). Move PIV to the cradle (3.9,0,2.0) and set Z0F = -(PIV.z - 0.1) = -1.9, so the collar is at x ≈ 3.9 (≈1.75 m ahead of the tracks). Optionally animate feed extension (feed slides 0.6 m down the cradle in t 0.15–0.20) so the foot is pushed onto the ground. Shift the first pattern row to x = 3.9.

findings.where: builder: hm/rod_ at local x=0 (feed-beam centreline); rock drill box 0.55 wide around 0.32 beam
findings.issue: The rock drill, shank, rods and bit lie on the centreline of the feed beam. In the vertical pose the drill string runs through the middle of the beam and the rock-drill box encloses the beam. On the class, the rock drill rides on a cradle on the front guides of the feed, and the string runs parallel to the beam about 0.3–0.4 m in front of it, through the centraliser/rod support at the feed foot.
findings.correction: Translate hm and rod_ (and the 'cent' centraliser box) by local x = +0.40 before applying ST. Local +x maps to world +x, away from the rig, when the feed is vertical. Rock drill box then spans 0.125–0.675 m from the beam axis and the rod sits at world x = PIV.x + 0.40. Add a cradle plate box (0.15, 0.5, 0.9) at local x = +0.20, z = ZH, joining the drill to the beam. Put the hole/collar of the active hole at x = PIV.x + 0.40.

findings.issue: In the stowed/start pose the 1.5 m of feed below the pivot and the centraliser block intersect the lower right corner of the cab (overlap y 0.15–0.30 over x 1.1–2.05).
findings.correction: Fixed by the boom/feed-extension change above: the feed is retracted up the cradle when stowed, so the foot sits ahead of x ≥ 2.3. If the boom is not added, set the stowed Z0F to -0.2 (feed retracted) and animate feed extension to -1.5 only once vertical, or offset the whole feed to y = -0.35 so it clears the cab (cab y ≥ 0.15).

findings.where: builder feed_ang/drill_s; FR=360; model_configuration 'animation … (12 s)'; principle step 5
findings.issue: (1) Drilling 3.4 m in 0.52 × 12 s ≈ 6.2 s is about 33 m/min, against 0.5–1.5 m/min (basis) to roughly 2 m/min in 20–80 MPa caprock. That is 20–60× compression, and it is not labelled. (2) Each cycle lays the feed flat forward (2 s raise, 1 s lower). Between holes on a pattern the rig lifts the foot off the ground and trams with the feed in the tramming position (near vertical or tilted back over the rig for stability). The feed is laid down only for transport. Step 5 ('the feed lowered, and the rig moves to the next hole') teaches the wrong practice. (3) The string does not rotate.
findings.correction: model_configuration.animation → 'Feed raised from transport position, rock drill drills ~3 m (time-compressed ≈ 30×; real penetration ≈ 0.5–1.5 m/min), string withdrawn, feed lifted to tramming position (12 s)'. Change the final segment: from t 0.92 lower only to D(70) (feed tilted back ~20° from vertical, foot clear of the ground) rather than to 0, or keep D(90) and raise the feed 0.3 m in its cradle. Step 5 → 'At design depth the string is withdrawn while flushing, the feed foot is lifted, the feed is put in the tramming position and the rig trams to the next hole.' Add string spin: rotate drill_string about its own axis at ~1 rev/s display rate during t 0.2–0.72 (real 60–150 rpm for top hammer).

findings.where: builder: bench box (18,20,0.3) at z -0.15 vs drill_s max 3.4 m
findings.issue: The bench is only 0.3 m thick while the bit drills 3.4 m. The string goes through the slab into empty space, and the model cannot show what the lesson teaches: caprock thickness, the caprock/ore contact and the sub-drill.
findings.correction: Build the bench as two layers: 'caprock' box (14, 17, 2.5) with top at z 0 (centre z -1.25), and below it a soft-ore layer (material bauxite/ore) (14, 17, 1.0) with centre z -3.0. Set the drill_s max to 3.0 (2.5 m caprock + 0.5 m sub-drill) and give the blast_pattern part section='front' so the cutaway shows the hole, contact and sub-drill. Fill cross_section.what_to_look_for: ['Hole through the caprock and ~0.5 m sub-drill into soft ore', 'Collar, stemming zone and charge column positions'].

findings.where: content params.hole_depth ('≈ 1–3.5 m'); params.fleet_reference_plant ('2'); plant.qty ('2')
findings.issue: The basis gives a hole depth of 1.5–5 m (benches 1–4 m) and a fleet of 2 operating + 1 standby, tag 01-DR-001…003. The lesson shows 1–3.5 m and qty '2', which conflicts with its own tag range.
findings.correction: hole_depth → P('Caprock thickness + ~0.3–0.5 m sub-drill (≈ 1.5–5 m)', '', 'Reference-plant design basis'). fleet_reference_plant → P('2 operating + 1 standby (3)', '', 'Reference-plant design basis'). plant.qty → '2 operating + 1 standby'.

findings.where: content params (compressor_flushing_air; missing penetration rate)
findings.issue: Only the top-hammer air pressure (~10 bar) is given, although the model is titled top-hammer/DTH and the basis gives 20–30 bar for DTH. Penetration rate (basis 0.5–1.5 m/min) and percussion frequency are not in the parameter table.
findings.correction: compressor_flushing_air → P('Top hammer ≈ 0.15–0.3 m³/s FAD at ~10–12 bar; DTH ≈ 0.3–0.5 m³/s at 20–30 bar (up-hole velocity ≥ ~15–25 m/s)', '', 'Class typical / basis'). Add 'penetration_rate': P('≈ 0.5 – 1.5', 'm/min', 'Reference-plant design basis (UCS 20–80 MPa)'); 'percussion_frequency': P('≈ 40 – 60 (top hammer); ≈ 15–30 (DTH)', 'Hz', 'Class typical').

findings.where: content failures
findings.issue: The two problems in the basis that affect charging are missing: hole collapse in clay-rich/broken ground, and water in holes during the monsoon. ANFO in wet holes desensitises, which causes misfires, poor breakage and NOx fume. The drill crew is the first to find both and must log them.
findings.correction: Add F('Hole collapse / blocked hole', ['Hole cannot be dipped to design depth', 'Cuttings fall back when the string is withdrawn'], ['Clay-rich or broken caprock, poor flushing, rain'], ['Clean out by redrilling; use hole liners/collar pipes or stemming plugs; log and flag for the shotfirer'], 'drill_string', 'quality') and F('Wet holes', ['Water at dip'], ['Groundwater/monsoon rain'], ['Log water depth; charge with emulsion (water-resistant), not ANFO; dewater holes/plan blast quickly'], 'drill_string', 'quality'). Add to key_points: 'Log every hole (depth, water, voids, caprock/ore contact); the shotfirer charges to the log.'

findings.where: content operation.alarms_interlocks, shut_down, start_up
findings.issue: The alarms and interlocks leave out the main drilling protections. The shut-down sequence leaves out compressor blow-down and parking away from the crest and blast area.
findings.correction: alarms_interlocks → ['Anti-jamming (high rotation pressure auto-retracts the feed)', 'Flushing-air pressure low/high (blocked bit or collapse)', 'Rod-handling and feed guard interlocks; cab-door/E-stop interlock on feed and percussion', 'Dust-collector differential pressure', 'Compressor discharge temperature', 'Hydraulic oil temperature/level, engine coolant', 'Tilt/levelling limits and tramming-with-feed-raised warning', 'Fire suppression']. shut_down → ['Withdraw the string while flushing, feed to tramming/transport position', 'Park on level ground away from the crest and outside any charged area', 'Unload the compressor and let it blow down, cool down the engine, engine off, isolate']. start_up → 'Warm up the engine and hydraulics, then load the compressor; test feed movement, anti-jamming and interlocks'.

findings.where: content maint (bit regrind 'as needed'; rock drill 'per percussion hours')
findings.issue: The maintenance intervals are too vague to teach. Ferricrete, often quartz-rich, is abrasive, and the bit regrind criterion is a core driller skill.
findings.correction: Bit: 'Regrind buttons before the wear flat reaches ~1/3 of the button diameter, or at the first sign of snakeskin/micro-cracks (typically every 20–80 m in abrasive caprock; track per bit)'. Rock drill: 'Check accumulator gas pre-charge every ~40–100 percussion hours; service/reseal per OEM (~400–600 h); overhaul ~1,000–1,500 h'. Add: 'Grease threads at every rod/bit change; replace shank adapter by wear/striking-face inspection'. Mark all as class-typical, per OEM.

findings.where: content definition ('lowers the centraliser to the ground'); principle step 2
findings.issue: The terminology is wrong. The feed foot (foot plate/stinger) is pressed onto the ground. The centraliser is the rod guide/support at the lower end of the feed that keeps the string on-line while collaring.
findings.correction: Definition: '… raises the feed to the design angle and pushes the feed foot onto the ground …'. Step 2: 'The feed is raised to vertical (design angle) and the feed foot is pressed onto the ground; the centraliser at the foot guides the rods while collaring.'

findings.where: builder: rod r=0.045 (90 mm), carousel rods 3.6 m vs 7 m string, bit r=0.06
findings.issue: A 90 mm rod in a ~120 mm hole leaves a very thin annulus. Class rods for 89–127 mm are T45/T51/GT60 (45–60 mm) or ST58/ST68 tube rods (~76 mm). The carousel rods (3.6 m) do not match the single ~7 m rod in the string.
findings.correction: Rod radius → 0.03 (GT60) for both the string and the carousel; bit radius → 0.0575 (115 mm). Make all rods 6.1 m (20 ft, Z0F+0.05 to Z0F+6.15 in the string; carousel rods 6.1 m, carousel box 6.3 m long), or use 3.66 m rods throughout. Holes ≤ 5 m are single-pass with a 6.1 m rod, so the carousel is optional for this duty.

findings.where: builder chassis; basis details_to_model
findings.issue: The basis asks for a collar dust hood with a suction hose to the dust collector, an exhaust stack, GNSS antennas and a beacon. The hood is what the lesson's dust-capture text describes, and it is missing.
findings.correction: Add a collar hood on the feed foot: cylinder r 0.30, z 0.05–0.40 at the rod position. Add a suction hose (sweep, r 0.07) from the hood to the dust collector inlet at (-0.1,-0.7,2.0). Add two GNSS antennas (cylinder r 0.08, h 0.05) on the cab roof and feed top, and an exhaust stack (r 0.07, z 3.0–3.6) at (-1.0, -0.5).

findings.where: quiz Q3, Q4, Q5; all answers index 0
findings.issue: Q3 says sub-drill is 'below the caprock'. Over soft bauxite only a short sub-drill is needed, and deep sub-drill into soft ore vents gas and dilutes the ore, which the quiz does not teach. Q4's distractors are trivial ('The rig colour'). Q5 is slightly inaccurate, because charging is done by a trained charging crew/MMU operator under the licensed shotfirer. Every correct answer is option 0, which is only a problem if the app does not shuffle.
findings.correction: Q3 explanation → 'A short sub-drill (~0.3–0.5 m) lets the charge break the full caprock without a hard toe; going deeper into soft ore wastes energy and dilutes ore.' Q4 options → ['The blast design (hole diameter, bench height, rock strength, fragmentation target)', 'The truck payload', 'The rig's tramming speed', 'The rod length']. Q5 answer → 'Trained charging crew under the licensed shotfirer, to the blast plan'. Randomise correct_option positions if the app does not shuffle.

findings.where: content applications[1]
findings.issue: 'Pre-split or trim holes where wall control is needed' does not fit 1–4 m caprock benches over free-dug ore, where there are no high final walls.
findings.correction: Replace with 'Secondary drilling of oversize boulders (where not broken by the rock breaker), and occasional hard ore lenses'.

review.overall_assessment:
The blast-hole drill model (m2p_blasthole_drill) is not ready for trainees. It shows the right class: a crawler top-hammer rig about 2.6 m wide and about 12.8 m long with the feed stowed, an 8.6 m feed, 89–127 mm holes, ~3 km/h tramming, a screw compressor, a dust collector and air-oil shank lubrication. The percussion frequency and the top-hammer vs DTH explanation are correct.

Main problems:
- Critical safety gap. The lesson never mentions old sockets or misfired holes, drilling near charged holes, overhead power lines, or stored energy in compressed air and accumulators.
- Wrong drill pattern. The 4 × 4 m pattern contradicts the design basis (3.0 × 3.5 m). It under-charges the caprock: about 0.25 kg/m³ against the basis 0.3–0.6 kg/m³.
- Wrong flushing-air path. The flow overlay sends air straight to the ground instead of down the rods and back up the hole to the dust hood.
- Missing boom. The feed pivots directly on the frame front. It passes through the frame, and in the stowed pose it clashes with the cab.
- String placement. The drill string runs through the centre of the feed beam instead of in front of it.
- Unrealistic animation. It is about 30× time-compressed without a label, and it lays the feed flat between holes instead of tramming with the feed up.
- Bench too thin. The bench is 0.3 m thick, so the bit drills into empty space.
- Numbers that conflict with the basis: hole depth and fleet size (should be 2 operating + 1 standby).
- Lesson gaps: no failure entries for wet holes or hole collapse, vague maintenance intervals, and thin alarms/interlocks.

Confidence is high on the geometry, consistency and safety findings, and medium on the class-typical numbers (air, intervals, rods).

findings.where: _eq_m2p_mine.py m2p_wheel_loader POSES (t=0.44 and t=0.52/0.62) and payload scale keys (t 0.48–0.54)
findings.issue: The animation never dumps. The absolute bucket angle is alpha + kap. At t=0.44 that is 46+46 = 92° rack-back, which leaves the lip pointing straight up and is impossible. At the 'dump' pose (t=0.52/0.62) it is 46−42 = +4°, so the bucket is still racked back slightly and the floor slopes up towards the lip. The payload just shrinks to 2 % between t=0.48 and 0.54 while the bucket stays level. A trainee would see material vanish from a level bucket.
findings.correction: Pose the bucket by its absolute angle: carry/full-lift rack-back about +50 to +60° absolute, dump −45° absolute (the SAE J732/ISO 7131 rated dump angle at max lift). Using the lift change in the next finding (alpha_max = 80°): t=0.22 (0, 0, D(45)); t=0.44 (D(28), D(80), D(-25)) for +55° abs; t=0.52 and 0.62 (D(30), D(80), D(-125)) for −45° abs. Start the load-scale ramp-down when kap passes about −95° (abs ≈ −15°, when material starts to slide) and finish it at −125°, not on a fixed 0.48–0.54 window.

findings.where: Z-bar linkage points B0=(4.55,2.9), C0=(4.95,2.0), D0=(5.95,1.95); _circ_int clamp
findings.issue: The four-bar B0–C–D–H cannot reach the dump range. Bell-crank lower arm = 0.985 m and link = 1.00 m give a reach of 0.016–1.986 m. |B0–D| goes past 1.986 m for any kap below about −20° relative (2.33 m at −40°, 3.63 m at −125°). _circ_int then clamps silently, so at the current dump pose (−42°) the bell crank and link come apart from the bucket pin and the tilt-cylinder length is meaningless. The Z-bar shown cannot dump.
findings.correction: Re-proportion the linkage. One set I checked as reachable across kap −125° to +50°, with transmission angle about 48–135° and bell-crank swing about 78°: B0=(4.55,2.75); D0=(6.15,1.55), bucket pin 0.63 m above/behind the hinge; R_BC=1.0 m; link R_CD=2.4 m; rest C0=(3.81,2.08) (lower branch). Change the pick to lambda p: p[1] < B0[1]. Put the bell-crank top opposite C about B, E0 ≈ (5.22,3.35), and keep F=(2.75,3.95), which gives a tilt cylinder about 2.5 m long with about 1.1 m stroke. Re-check visually after the change.

findings.where: lift arm A=(2.3,3.4), H=(6.35,0.95); POSES alpha max D(46)
findings.issue: Arm length is 4.73 m and lift is only 46°, so the hinge pin reaches about 4.6 m at 'full lift'. With the lip about 2.1–2.2 m below the hinge at a 45° dump, dump clearance is only about 2.4 m. That is well short of the stated 4.5–5 m and below the side-board height of a 90 t truck (~4.1–4.4 m). The 'full lift' render shows the bucket barely above the cab. Class hinge-pin height at max lift is about 6.8–7.1 m.
findings.correction: Raise the full-lift arm rotation to alpha = D(80): the arm goes from −31° to +49° and the hinge pin reaches 6.96 m. Dump clearance then comes out at about 4.7–4.8 m at 45°. Lift-cylinder length goes from 2.92 m to 4.22 m (1.3 m stroke, ratio 1.45, which is feasible). For the post-dump 'carry' pose use alpha ≈ D(10–15) instead of D(6).

findings.where: bucket profile bpts / WB=2.55
findings.issue: Measured from the profile, the bucket cross-section is about 3.14 m², so struck ≈ 15.7 m³ and heaped (2:1) ≈ 20 m³ at 5.1 m width. The label says 11–12 m³, so the bucket is about 70 % oversized.
findings.correction: Scale bpts about the heel point (H[0]−0.25, 0.08) by s ≈ 0.77 in x and z. That gives floor about 1.55 m and back height about 1.7 m, heaped about 11.5–12 m³ per ISO 7546. Keep the width at 5.1 m. Also move the hinge bosses and the D0 pin so they stay on the scaled bucket back.

findings.where: hitch part (steering cylinders sc±1), never keyframed
findings.issue: The steering cylinders are static while the front frame rotates up to 30° about the hitch. Their front eyes come away from the front frame, and neither cylinder extends or retracts. This is the very mechanism the lesson highlights (principle step 3 targets 'hitch').
findings.correction: Make each steering cylinder a barrel/rod pair. Pin the barrel to the rear frame at (−0.9, ±0.85, 1.55) and keyframe the rod eye to Rz(phi)·(0.9, ±0.85, 1.55). At phi=+30° the left cylinder retracts to about 1.30 m and the right extends to about 2.18 m (from 1.80 m). Leave only the hitch pins and plate static.

findings.where: content params.rated_payload / bucket_load label 'Bucket load (~20 t)' / basis 'Bucket payload 15–18 t'
findings.issue: The figures don't agree. The lesson says 20–22 t per pass and the model labels the load ~20 t, while the basis says 15–18 t. With an 11–12 m³ bucket in loose bauxite (~1.5–1.7 t/m³, ~90–95 % fill) the real pass is about 16–18 t. 20 t would need about 1.8 t/m³ or a ~13 m³ bucket.
findings.correction: Keep 'rated_payload ≈ 20 – 22 t (machine rating, class envelope)'. Add 'bucket_payload_bauxite': P('≈ 16 – 18', 't per pass', '11–12 m³ × ~1.6 t/m³ loose × ~0.95 fill; engineering estimate'). Rename the part to 'Bucket load (~17 t bauxite)' and change META wl_load to 'About 16–18 t of bauxite per pass (rated payload ~21–22 t)'.

findings.where: params.engine_power '650–750 kW'; META wl_rear and rear_frame label '~700 kW class'; basis '~600–650 kW'
findings.issue: Three different engine powers for one machine. For the 992/WA900 class, net flywheel power is about 600–650 kW and gross about 650–700 kW. 750 kW is above the class.
findings.correction: Lesson: engine_power P('≈ 600 – 700', 'kW', 'Class envelope (net–gross)'). META and part label: 'engine (~650 kW class)'. Keep the basis at 600–650 kW net, or widen it to the same 600–700 kW net–gross wording.

findings.where: content plant.qty '1' and params.fleet_reference_plant '1' vs tag 01-FL-001…002 and basis
findings.issue: The basis lists 1 operating + 1 standby (fleet summary: '2 x ~100-t wheel loaders (1 standby)'), and the excavator standby is set to 0 because the loader provides cover. The lesson says 1 unit while the tag range covers two.
findings.correction: plant.qty = '2 installed (1 operating + 1 standby)'. fleet_reference_plant = P('2 (1 op + 1 standby)', '', 'Reference-plant design basis').

findings.where: content safety[] (2 items only)
findings.issue: The safety content leaves out several of the main hazards for this class, including ones already in the basis (tyre explosion/nitrogen inflation, reversing). Missing: tyre heat/pyrolysis exclusion, raised-arm stored energy, machine fire, three-point access, edge/windrow and bench-face risks.
findings.correction: Add: 'Tyres: inflate with nitrogen only; after any heat event (fire, lightning strike, welding/heating near the rim, brake overheating) set the OEM/site tyre exclusion zone (typically ≥300 m in front of the tread, ~50+ m to the side) for at least 24 h'; 'Never work under raised arms or bucket — lower to the ground or fit the lift-arm support/lock and isolate stored hydraulic energy'; 'Fire: hot turbo/exhaust plus hydraulic or fuel leaks; keep the fire-suppression system armed and know the manual actuator'; 'Use three points of contact on stairs; never mount or dismount a moving machine'; 'Stay off windrows and bench edges; keep the bucket low when travelling; sound the horn before moving (1 forward, 2 reverse)'.

findings.where: content operation.pre_start / start_up / shut_down / alarms_interlocks
findings.issue: The steps are too thin for operator training. Pre-start has no fluid levels or fire-suppression check. Start-up has no brake hold test. Shut-down has no parking-location rule and no implement lockout. The interlock list is incomplete.
findings.correction: pre_start: add 'Check engine, transmission, hydraulic and coolant levels; fire-suppression armed; lights, horn, cameras and radar working; isolation tags removed; tyres cold-checked'. start_up: add 'Neutral and park brake on before cranking; let the automatic secondary-steering check complete; do the service- and park-brake holding tests per OEM/site procedure before leaving the parking area'. shut_down: 'Park on level ground clear of traffic, highwalls and edges; bucket flat on the ground; transmission in neutral; park brake on; implement lockout engaged; cool-down idle (~3–5 min); engine off; three-point dismount'. alarms_interlocks: add 'Neutral-start interlock', 'Low brake-accumulator pressure → automatic park-brake application', 'Implement (hydraulic) lockout', 'Fire-suppression discharge / engine shutdown', 'Payload overload warning'.

findings.where: content failures[]
findings.issue: The most consequential failure modes for this class are missing: machine fire, overheating of the torque converter and brakes from stall and wheel spin in the pile, and structural cracking of the loader tower/arms. META lists radiator blockage but the lesson does not.
findings.correction: Add F('Machine fire', ['Smoke, fire-suppression alarm'], ['Hydraulic/fuel leak onto turbo or exhaust, debris build-up'], ['Hose inspection, wash-downs, fire-suppression service'], 'rear_frame', 'fire'). Add F('Power-train overheating', ['High torque-converter or brake oil temperature'], ['Prolonged stall or wheel spin in the pile, riding the brakes, blocked cores'], ['Use the impeller clutch/rimpull control, clean the cooling cores, keep the floor clean'], 'rear_frame', 'thermal'). Add F('Structural cracking', ['Cracks at the tower, arm or cross-tube welds'], ['Shock loading, prying with the bucket'], ['NDT at major services, do not pry or ram'], 'lift_arms', 'structure').

findings.where: content selection[] 'load the haul trucks in ~5–6 passes'
findings.issue: OEM loader–truck matching for wheel loaders is about 3–5 passes. A 992 class loader is normally matched to a 90 t truck in about 4 passes at rated payload, and 6 passes means the loader is undersized for the truck. The selection text also never mentions that low-density bauxite is why a light-material bucket may be the better choice.
findings.correction: 'Match the loader to the truck in ~4–5 passes. In low-density bauxite (~1.6 t/m³ loose) an 11–12 m³ rock bucket gives ~17 t and about 5 passes into a 90 t truck. Consider a ~13–14 m³ bucket for ore-only duty to use the ~21 t rated payload, and keep a rock bucket for ferricrete caprock.'

findings.where: RT=1.55 (tyre OD 3.1 m); params.tyres '~3 m diameter'; basis key_dimensions
findings.issue: A 45/65R45 L-5 tyre is about 2.85–2.9 m OD, so the model tyre is about 7 % oversized. That also raises the frame and pivot heights.
findings.correction: Set RT = 1.44 (OD ≈ 2.88 m). Change the wording to '45/65R45 class, ~2.9 m diameter'. Keep the wheelbase at 5.8 m and lower the fenders to RT*2+0.15.

findings.where: rr K.stair 'rst' at x = −6.55 behind the counterweight
findings.issue: The basis details_to_model asks for front access stairs next to the cab. The model instead has a stairway at the extreme rear that reaches down to 0.45 m. In real machines that position would be struck when reversing into the pile or windrow, and it cuts the departure angle.
findings.correction: Move the main access to a diagonal stairway on the left side of the rear frame, from about (−0.8, 1.9, 0.6) up to the cab platform at about (−2.4, 1.6, 2.75), with a handrail. Keep at most a rear ladder on the grille side for engine-deck access, with its bottom rung ≥0.6 m above ground.

findings.where: content key_points 'Z-bar linkage: strong breakout, bucket racks back as it lifts'; quiz Q2 explanation
findings.issue: 'Racks back as it lifts' is misleading. Z-bar is not parallel-lift, so the bucket angle drifts as the arms rise and the operator corrects it with tilt; rack-back is a deliberate tilt action. The Q2 explanation also leaves out the main reason for high breakout.
findings.correction: Key point: 'Z-bar linkage: high breakout because rack-back uses the full-bore (head) side of the tilt cylinder through the bell crank; not parallel-lift, so the operator trims bucket angle while lifting (return-to-dig and lift kick-out set the positions)'. Q2 explanation: 'Rack-back is powered by the tilt cylinder's head side, multiplied by the bell crank near ground level.'

findings.where: content key_points load-and-carry; operation.normal
findings.issue: The text gives no number for 'short distance'. Blending on the ROM pad is load-and-carry from the grade-bin fingers to the hopper, so the trainee needs a limit, and tyre TKPH is the controlling check.
findings.correction: 'Keep load-and-carry short — typically ≤100–150 m (ROM-pad fingers laid out within this distance of the hopper); check tyre TKPH for the shift; travel with the bucket low (~0.5 m) and racked back.'

findings.where: content maint.periodic / routine
findings.issue: Every oil and filter service is lumped into '250–500 h', and the basic daily checks found in OEM schedules are missing.
findings.correction: Split out: oil sampling (engine, transmission, hydraulic, axles) every 250 h; engine oil and filters 500 h; transmission and hydraulic filters 500 h; transmission oil about 2,000 h; hydraulic oil about 4,000 h (or condition-based). Add daily cold tyre pressures and wheel-nut checks, cleaning of the cooling cores, and fire-suppression inspection (monthly plus 6-monthly service).

findings.where: META model_configuration.animation; POSES
findings.issue: The machine never travels. Filling happens without driving into the pile, and the 13 s loop is not labelled as compressed compared with the 35–45 s cycle in the lesson.
findings.correction: Add front- and rear-frame translation: +2 m into the pile over t 0.08–0.22, −6 m reverse while articulating over t 0.22–0.40, then +4 m to the target over t 0.40–0.50. Alternatively, keep it stationary and change the animation note to '…return (13 s, time-compressed; real V-cycle ~35–45 s; travel omitted)'.

findings.where: content quiz[]
findings.issue: All four questions are recall questions with obvious distractors ('It is illegal', 'The bucket falls off'), and none covers the critical safety content.
findings.correction: Replace Q4's distractors with plausible ones ('It overheats the hydraulic oil', 'It wears the bucket teeth faster', 'It reduces breakout force'). Add Q('Before working between the front and rear frames you must…', ['Fit the steering frame-lock link and isolate the machine', 'Articulate fully to one side', 'Raise the bucket for clearance', 'Leave the engine idling'], 0, 'The articulation pinch point is fatal; the frame lock prevents steering movement.').

review.overall_assessment:
The wheel loader is the right class overall. Length is about 15.4 m, wheelbase 5.8 m, width about 4.75 m over the tyres, cab top about 5.9 m and bucket width 5.1 m, all consistent with a 992/WA900 class machine. The component set is correctly named (oscillating rear axle and fixed front, centre hitch, Z-bar with one tilt cylinder, rear cooling, counterweight). The lesson's steering, Z-bar and ROM-pad blending explanations are basically sound.

The core loading kinematics are wrong, though. The Z-bar four-bar cannot reach any bucket rotation below about −20° relative, so the linkage comes apart at the 'dump' pose. The bucket is racked back 92° at lift and only +4° at 'dump', so the payload disappears from a level bucket. Arm lift (46°, hinge 4.6 m) gives about 2.4 m dump clearance instead of the stated 4.5–5 m, so the model visibly cannot load a 90 t truck. The steering cylinders do not animate. The bucket profile is about 20 m³ heaped against an 11–12 m³ label.

The numbers also disagree across lesson, META and basis: engine power 600–650, 650–750 and ~700 kW; payload 20–22 t vs 15–18 t; fleet quantity 1 vs 1+1. Safety, operating procedure and failure-mode content are too thin for operator training (tyre exclusion zones, raised-arm stored energy, fire, interlocks). The geometry fixes above give numbers I checked in the scratchpad (the linkage set is reachable across −125° to +50°, and an 80° lift puts the hinge at 6.96 m). Confidence is high on the kinematic and consistency findings and medium on class figures (power, tyre OD, hinge height, pass matching), which come from memory without web access.

findings.where: _eq_m2p_mine.py m2p_mine_overview: terr['ramp'] extrude_poly(..., 46, 58) and haul_road berms (berms only on road_pts[1:] segments)
findings.issue: The pit access ramp has no windrow or edge bund. Its pit-side edge (y = 46) is an open drop of 0 to 7 m to the pit floor along the whole 70 m ramp, and the haul-road berms start only at the ramp top. Ramp edge protection is a fatal-risk control: vehicles going over an open edge. The model teaches the opposite of what the road label says ('safety berms ≥ half tyre height').
findings.correction: Add a windrow on the open (pit-side) edge of the ramp along its full length. Use a trapezoid section: 1.4 m high (≥ half the 27.00R49 tyre diameter, about 1.35 m), base about 4.5 m, crest about 0.5 m. Follow the ramp grade from (-68, y_edge, -7.0) to (2, y_edge, 0.0), then carry it on into the haul-road berms without a gap. Add the line 'Ramps and haul roads have windrows ≥ half the tyre height of the largest vehicle on every open edge' to the safety list.

findings.where: terr['ramp'] (width y 46–58 = 12 m) and the loop path 'simplified, same lane'
findings.issue: The ramp is 12 m wide, which is single-lane for a ~6.1 m-wide 90 t truck. Trucks run up and down it in both directions on the same centreline. The META entry mn_road says two-lane 22–25 m. The ramp also sits inside the mined block (y 46–58 of a pit that spans ±60) and ends at z = 0 above a bench at z = -1.3, leaving a 1.3 m step at the top.
findings.correction: Make the ramp two-lane: running width ≥ 3–3.5 × truck width, about 21–22 m, plus the windrow and drain, about 25–27 m overall. Cut it into the pit side wall outside the mined block. For example, add an undisturbed plateau strip y = 60–100 along the model and build the ramp at y = 62–88 from (-68, -7.0) to (2, 0.0), so its top meets the plateau at z = 0. Offset the outbound and return truck paths by ±5.5 m from the centreline and keep left or right consistently with the site's traffic rule.

findings.where: Truck keyframes: loop (out-and-back on one polyline), phase offsets k/4, FR = 600
findings.issue: I computed the paths. Because the loop is out-and-back on one line with quarter offsets, pairs of trucks reach zero separation four times per cycle and pass through each other head-on. Trucks 1 and 3 coincide at frame 0, so the thumbnail and rest pose show two trucks merged on the ramp. The round trip is 598 m in 20 s, an average of about 108 km/h, including a loaded climb up the 10 % ramp. There is no stop for spotting, loading or tipping.
findings.correction: Use separate outbound and return lanes offset ±5.5 m, so trucks never share a lane head-on. Phase the trucks 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 along a closed circuit rather than an out-and-back line. Raise FR to about 3,600 frames (120 s), giving about 18 km/h average, or label the clip 'time-compressed ~6×' in model_configuration. Add dwell keyframes: about 2.5 s spotting and loading under the excavator and about 3 s reversing and tipping at the hopper. Typical speeds are 10–12 km/h loaded up a 10 % ramp and 30–40 km/h on the flat.

findings.where: loop points (32,148,0)→(40,148,1)→(52,148,10)→(58,150,10) and the return; sizing_station instance at (60,160,0)
findings.issue: Getting onto the tipping deck: the truck climbs 9 m in 12 m (a 75 % grade) straight through the station's MSE wall block and its truncated ramp stub. The stub ends in an 8.6 m vertical drop at world x = 26. The truck drives forward along the deck parallel to the hopper, turns 180° instantly and drives off without reversing to the wheel stop or tipping. That is the wrong way to dump with a rear-dump truck.
findings.correction: In the overview, extend the station's ramp at 10 %: from local (-34, 8.6) down to (-120, 0), 28 m wide (matching the deck), with windrows. Join the haul road to its foot. On the deck, keyframe a turn, then a reverse perpendicular to the hopper edge (heading ±y) until the rear tyres are about 1 m short of the 1.35 m wheel-stop bund at local y = ±5.0. Then play the truck's body-raise clip (about 13.5 s) before it drives off.

findings.where: rom_pad: box 70×40 m at (10,165) and five fingers 8 × 16 × 4.5 m half-ellipses at x = -15…25
findings.issue: The ROM pad covers 0.28 ha. The design basis gives 4–6 ha. The five half-ellipse fingers hold about 3 kt in total, roughly 4–5 h of a ~17 kt/day ROM rate, so they cannot work as a blending reserve. A half-ellipse has vertical sides at the toe, which is impossible for bauxite with a 35–38° angle of repose. The pad box (x up to 45) and the finger at x = 25 overlap the station's +y ramp footprint (world x 26–40, y 164.7–192.7). The haul road's last segment (x 21–43, y 115–140) runs into the side of the −y ramp (y 127–155).
findings.correction: Move the pad clear of the station ramps and haul road, for example centred at (10, 225) with the fingers in y 205–245. Use trapezoid finger sections: base 22 m, crest 2 m, height 7 m (about 35–37° sides), about 60–80 m long. That is about 8–10 kt each and 40–50 kt for five fingers, roughly 2.5–3 days' ROM. Set the pad to at least 200 × 150 m (3 ha). If the scene cannot hold that, add the label 'ROM pad shown reduced; design 4–6 ha'. Put one wheel loader (link m2p_wheel_loader) on the pad reclaiming a finger.

findings.where: terr['backfill'] bfo 5.5 m and terr['rehab'] rho 5.6 m laterite; vertical backfill wall at x = -70
findings.issue: Mass balance: only 1.3 m of topsoil and overburden (plus 1.5 m of caprock if it is treated as waste) is removed above 4.2 m of ore. Yet the model backfills 5.5–5.6 m of laterite and leaves the rehabilitated surface only 1.1–1.4 m below the original plateau. With the stated strip ratio of 0.3–0.6 that is not possible. In real practice the rehabilitated pit stays a shallow depression roughly as deep as the ore removed. The loose backfill also stands as a vertical 5.7 m wall facing the active pit.
findings.correction: Set the backfill and rehab overburden thickness to about (removed overburden + waste caprock) × swell 1.2–1.3 = 1.6–3.6 m, for example 2.5 m. The rehabilitated surface then sits at about -4.5 m with topsoil 0.15–0.3 m on top. Batter the rehab and backfill edges: 37° (angle of repose) at the active-pit contact (toe about 7.6 m out from the crest), and final landform walls at ≤ 15–20°, blending into the surrounding plateau. Add a note: 'Rehabilitated pits are left as shallow depressions; ore removed is not replaced.'

findings.where: content MODULES['m2p_mine_overview'].definition
findings.issue: 'Mining advances from the forest (right) toward the left' is backwards. The code comment says mining advances toward +x, and in the model the face moves right, into the forest. The right-to-left order in space is the sequence in time, not the direction the face moves. A trainee will get the advance direction wrong.

review.overall_assessment:
Reviewer: bauxite mining engineer (plateau strip mining, grade control, rehabilitation). Web search was unavailable, so this relies on my own knowledge. Confidence is high on the geometry and animation findings, which I checked by computing paths and coordinates from the builder code, and medium on the practice numbers.

The overview gets the concept right: the clearing → stripping → caprock drill and blast → ore to the clay floor → backfill → rehabilitation sequence, the five-layer lateritic profile (thicknesses in range: ore 4.2 m, caprock 1.5 m), the 10 % ramp grade, the berm height on the road, the ROM tonnage (6.2–6.4 Mt/yr), grade targets, strip ratio and rehabilitation rate all match the reference-plant design basis. The quiz has one clearly correct answer per question.

The model is not yet fit for trainees, for these reasons:
1. **Critical safety gap:** the pit ramp has an open 0–7 m edge with no windrow.
2. **Ramp:** it is 12 m wide (single-lane) but carries two-way traffic on one centreline.
3. **Truck animation:** trucks pass through each other (two are merged at frame 0), average about 108 km/h, climb a 75 % grade through the station's concrete walls, and drive forward along the tipping deck and U-turn instead of reversing and tipping.
4. **Layout clashes:** the ROM pad is 0.28 ha against a 4–6 ha basis and overlaps the station ramp and haul road; its stockpiles have vertical sides.
5. **Backfill:** the backfill thickness breaks mass balance, and the loose backfill stands as a vertical wall.
6. **Wording:** the definition states the mining advance direction backwards.
7. **Missing content:** no grade-control element at all and no drill rig, even though the lesson centres on both.
8. **Template text:** the generated tours describe 'liquid from suction to discharge', a cutaway and an exploded view, none of which apply.
9. **Operation and safety:** start-up and shut-down are missing, and safety is a single line.
10. **References:** the closure standard cited (GISTM) is wrong.
11. **Deposit type:** the content mixes Darling Range-style (thin ore, jarrah forest) and East Coast India-style (40 % available Al₂O₃) deposits. The design basis flags this itself.

Fixing the ramp, traffic, station approach, ROM pad and backfill geometry, and adding grade-control and drill content, would bring this to a good teaching standard.

findings.where: content/m2p_mine.py MODULES['m2p_blasthole_drill'].safety, operation.normal, failures; META dr_pattern
findings.issue: The drill lesson leaves out the safety rules that kill drillers. It never says not to drill into or next to old sockets (butts) or misfired holes, even though the design basis lists that hazard. It gives no separation from a charged pattern, no crest stand-off, no lightning rule for charged holes, and no whip checks on air hoses. Its only blasting line is 'Blast exclusion zones after charging; misfire procedures', with no numbers. Respirable crystalline silica is mentioned only as 'dust'.
findings.correction: Add to safety: (1) 'Never drill into, or within ~0.5 m of, an old socket (butt) or a hole that may hold explosive. Inspect the bench for butts before collaring; any suspected misfire is reported to the shotfirer and the area is barricaded.' (2) 'Do not drill within the site separation distance of charged holes; drilling stops once charging of the pattern starts.' (3) 'Keep the tracks at least 2–3 m (site rule) from a crest; tram at right angles to the edge.' (4) 'Lightning warning (detector or site alert) → stop charging, clear the blast area and the charged pattern to the exclusion distance.' (5) 'Whip checks on all air couplings; depressurise before breaking a connection.' (6) 'Respirable crystalline silica: collar hood and dust collector working, water injection, pressurised cab, P2 respirator outside the cab.' Add F('Drilling into a misfire/butt', ['Explosive residue or a socket at the collar'], ['Butts not marked after the last blast'], ['Stop, do not withdraw the rods, evacuate, call the shotfirer; post-blast inspection marks all butts'], 'drill_string', 'safety'). Give numbers in safety: 'Exclusion typically ≥ 300–500 m for people and ≥ 100–200 m for equipment (machines facing away), as the site blast plan sets.'
