findings.where: _eq_m2p_mine.py m2p_wheel_loader POSES (t 0.44: arm 46°, bucket +46°; t 0.52: bucket −42°); A=(2.3,3.4), H=(6.35,0.95)
findings.issue: The bucket's world angle is arm angle + bucket angle. At 'dump' this is 46° − 42° = +4°, so the bucket is level with the lip slightly up and never tips, and the load mesh simply shrinks away. At full lift the hinge pin is only about 4.6 m high (the arm is 4.73 m long and lifted 46°). A 45° dump would therefore have the lip at about 2.8 m, which is below the ~4.4–4.6 m body rail of the A01 haul truck and the class dump clearance of 4.5–5 m given in the same lesson. Before the dump the bucket is racked back to +92° world, which would spill the load over the arms.
findings.correction: Set full lift to an arm angle of about 78° (hinge pin ≈ 6.9 m; class ≈ 6.5–7 m, medium confidence; the lift-cylinder stroke ratio stays ≈ 1.44). Dump pose: bucket relative angle = −(78 + 45)° = −123°, giving a world angle of −45°. Carry/lift pose: bucket relative angle = −(arm angle) + 45°, keeping about 45° of world rack-back. Verify that _circ_int stays solvable; if not, lengthen the arms (H rest at (6.6, 0.95)). Check that the lip clearance at a 45° dump is ≥ 4.7 m. Start the load scale-down only after the world bucket angle passes −25°.

findings.where: basis A01 equipment[9] key_dimensions[2] ('wheel stop ~1.2–1.4 m'); content key_points/params wheel_stop_height ('≥ ~1.35'); wheel_loader lesson (loader tips into 01-HP)
findings.issue: The wheel stop is sized for half of the 2.7 m truck tyre. The rule is half the wheel height of the LARGEST machine that uses the dump point, and the ~3.1 m-tyred wheel loader also reclaims from the ROM pad into this hopper (and tips at ROM fingers). The basis range of 1.2–1.4 m also allows values below its own half-tyre rule.
findings.correction: Set the wheel stop and windrows at all tipping points used by the loader to ≥ 1.55 m (half of the ~3.1 m 45/65R45 tyre), or provide a separate loader tip point. Change the basis to '≥ ½ the wheel height of the largest machine using the dump (≥ 1.35 m trucks only; ≥ 1.55 m if the loader tips here)'. Update params.wheel_stop_height and quiz Q3 wording to say 'largest machine'. In the builder set ws height to 1.55 m.

findings.where: content principle step 5, operation.normal[2] ('reverse square to the edge or hopper'), install.haul_road_and_dump_design; basis RP hazards ('use tip-and-push')
findings.issue: The lesson teaches reversing square to 'the edge' for every dump. At the ROM-pad fingers (6–8 m high) and at waste/backfill dumps, edge tipping causes most truck roll-overs over dump crests. The basis specifies tip-and-push (paddock dumping) for the ROM pad.
findings.correction: Change normal[2] to: 'At the hopper: reverse square to the wheel stop. On the ROM pad and on waste/backfill dumps: tip short of the crest (paddock dump, or tip-and-push so the dozer pushes the load over), or reverse only to a windrow at least ½ tyre height that has been inspected that shift; never reverse to an unprotected edge; stay off cracked or soft crests (report them).' Mirror this in principle step 5 and add a quiz question with this answer.

findings.where: content MODULES['m2p_mine_overview'].safety (one line), operation.alarms_interlocks
findings.issue: The area lesson is where trainees learn the site-wide hazards, but it has only one safety line. It leaves out the traffic management plan and right-of-way, light-vehicle/heavy-vehicle segregation and collision avoidance (the basis's top fatality risk), fatigue, lightning and storm stop-work on an exposed plateau, slippery haul roads after rain or over-watering, runaway escape lanes on plateau-to-valley grades, drowning in sumps and sediment ponds, dust and silica, and the blast clearance sequence.
findings.correction: Replace safety with: 'Traffic management plan: one-way loops where possible, give-way rules, heavy vehicles have right of way; light vehicles need a buggy whip, beacon, radio call-up and CAS and never park in a truck's blind zone'; 'Fatigue management: shift design, fatigue monitoring on trucks'; 'Lightning/storm: stop work on exposed benches and decks and clear any charged blast pattern when the lightning alert sounds'; 'Wet roads: reduce speed limits, grade and drain, never heavily water ramps or intersections'; 'Escape lanes or arrester berms on long downgrades; brake test before descending'; 'Sumps and ponds: fenced, signed, life rings, no lone work'; 'Blasting: sirens, guard posts, all-clear before re-entry, post-blast inspection'; 'Dust: water carts, cab pressurisation, silica monitoring'. Add to alarms_interlocks: 'Lightning detection alert', 'Fatigue alarm', 'Overspeed alarm via FMS'.

findings.where: content MODULES['m2p_wheel_loader'].safety (2 lines), operation.normal/alarms_interlocks
findings.issue: The loader reverses on every V-cycle and works mixed with trucks on the ROM pad. The lesson leaves out reversing-collision controls, ROM-pad traffic rules, the 300 m tyre-fire/explosion exclusion (which the basis lists for this machine), hopper tipping rules (traffic light, no tipping while the breaker works) and fire suppression.
findings.correction: Add to safety: 'Reversing is the main loader hazard — camera/radar, proximity detection, never reverse into a truck lane; ROM pad uses a one-way truck loop and the loader works only on its marked side'; 'Hot or burning tyre, power-line contact or lightning strike: evacuate, ≥ 300 m exclusion (as for trucks)'; 'At the dump hopper: tip only on green, square to the wheel stop, never while the rock breaker is working'; 'Fire suppression fitted; clean the engine bay'. Add to alarms_interlocks: 'Proximity detection / CAS', 'Fire-suppression actuation', 'Steering/secondary-steering pressure'.

findings.where: m2p_blasthole_drill FR = 360, drill_s(t) 3.4 m over t 0.2–0.72; m2p_wheel_loader FR = 390; META model_configuration.animation
findings.issue: The drill animation drills 3.4 m in about 6 s, roughly 33 m/min against the 0.5–1.5 m/min in the basis (20–60 times too fast), and raises the feed in 1.8 s. The loader cycle takes 13 s against the stated 35–45 s V-cycle. The truck, excavator and dozer were moved to real time, so these two now teach wrong speeds without saying so.
findings.correction: Drill: keep FR = 360 but label model_configuration.animation 'time-compressed ≈ 30× (real penetration 0.5–1.5 m/min; a 3 m hole ≈ 3–5 min)', and show a 'time-compressed' badge in the viewer. Loader: set FR = 1,200 (40 s real time) with the POSES times unchanged as fractions, or label it 'time-compressed ≈ 3×'.

findings.where: content: truck applications[0] ('ore and caprock … to the primary sizer'), excavator fleet ('1 on caprock/overburden'), sizer failures ('large slabs of caprock'), overview mn_blasted ('loaded as ore where grade allows'); basis open_questions[4]
findings.issue: The lessons contradict each other on whether caprock is ore or waste: the truck and sizer lessons treat it as ore, the excavator lesson as overburden. The basis lists this as an open question. The answer changes strip ratio, sizer duty (hard ferricrete wears teeth), dilution and drill-and-blast quantity.
findings.correction: State one rule in all lessons and in the basis: 'Caprock is classified by grade-control assay: where available Al₂O₃ and reactive SiO₂ meet the ore cut-off it is hauled to the sizer as ore (Darling-Range practice); otherwise it goes to backfill as waste. Reference plant: assume ~50 % of caprock is ore (to be confirmed).' Use the same sentence in the truck applications, the excavator fleet note ('1 on caprock/waste'), sizer failures and the overview key points.

findings.where: content params.fleet_reference_plant ('1') / plant qty '1' vs tag 01-FL-001…002; m2p_blasthole_drill fleet '2' / qty '2' vs tag 01-DR-001…003; basis FL 1+1, DR 2+1; overview params
findings.issue: Fleet numbers contradict the tags and the basis, as the dozer did before it was fixed. For the loader this matters operationally: the basis has no standby excavator because 'the wheel loader provides cover'. A single loader cannot cover a downed excavator and keep up ROM-pad blending (20–40 % rehandle) at the same time.
findings.correction: Loader: P('2 (1 operating + 1 standby / back-up loading)', '', 'Reference-plant design basis'); plant qty '1 operating + 1 standby'. Drill: P('3 (2 operating + 1 standby)', …); plant qty '2 operating + 1 standby'. Add an overview parameter 'fleet_reference_plant': 'EX 3 · HT 9 + 2 · DZ 3 + 1 · DR 2 + 1 · FL 1 + 1 · GR 1–2 · WC 2 · RC 1–2 (design basis)' so trainees see the whole fleet in one place.

findings.where: content MODULES['m2p_hydraulic_excavator'].selection[0] ('Size the bucket to the truck (4–5 passes)')
findings.issue: A '4–5 passes' figure is left over in the excavator selection text. Everything else (definition, params, quiz, truck lesson, basis) now says 5–6 passes at ~15–17 t.
findings.correction: Change it to 'Size the bucket to the truck (about 5–6 passes of ~15–17 t in bauxite) and to the required tonnes per hour; diesel suits a moving plateau pit (no trailing cable).'

findings.where: A01 catalogue (7 models) vs basis equipment list (01-RC, 01-RP, 01-GR/WC, 01-PP/SP, 01-SV, 01-MIA)
findings.issue: Several equipment items and processes a bauxite-mine trainee must understand have no model or lesson, and the existing lessons refer to some of them as if they did (01-RC, 01-RP, water carts).
findings.correction: Add, in this priority order: (1) a ROM pad and blending model (01-RP): finger piles with grade-bin signboards, windrows, one-way truck loop, loader reclaim to the hopper, direct-tip 60–80 %; own model. (2) A grade-control RC/aircore rig with cyclone, splitter and sample bags (01-RC), whose lesson explains available Al₂O₃ and reactive SiO₂ (low-temperature 143–150 °C micro-digest) and QAQC; own model. (3) A blasting-cycle process lesson: dip and log holes, MMU charging (emulsion in wet holes), stemming, tie-in, clearance and guards, firing, post-blast and misfire handling; reuse the drill's blast_pattern part plus a simple MMU model. (4) A water cart (90 t chassis with tank, spray bar and cannon) and a motor grader, which control rolling resistance, dust and fire response; own models, the cart can reuse the truck chassis. (5) A diesel dry-prime dewatering pump and sediment pond (01-PP/SP), a natural fit for PumpForge; own model. (6) A tyre handler and tyre-change procedure (stored-energy hazard); lower priority. Light vehicles go in the overview, not as their own model.

findings.where: m2p/basis/draft_A01_A02_A03.json A01 equipment[3], [4], [5], [9], [11]; META ex_upper, ex_bucket
findings.issue: The design basis was not updated after the lesson fixes, so the two disagree. Truck gross power: basis 700–760 kW, lesson 750–900. Sizer throughput: basis '2,000–2,500 (design)', lesson 1,800 design / 2,000–2,400 rated. Deck height: basis '8–10 m above apron feeder', model ≈ 6 m above the pans and 10 m above grade. Excavator tail swing: basis ~6 m, lesson 5.3–5.6 m, META ex_upper '5–5.5 m'. Loader power: basis 600–650 kW, lesson 650–750 kW. META ex_bucket also says 'Tooth loss → crusher damage' although the station has a sizer.
findings.correction: Change the basis entries to: truck '~750–900 kW gross (reference ~750)'; sizer 'design flow 1,800 t/h; rated 2,000–2,400 t/h'; dump station 'tipping deck ≈ 10 m above grade (≈ 6 m above the feeder pans)'; excavator 'tail swing ~5.3–5.6 m'; loader and lesson both '≈ 600–700 kW (class)'. Change META ex_upper to '~5.3–5.6 m' and ex_bucket to 'Tooth loss → sizer damage'.

findings.where: labels['forest'] ('jarrah-type forest'); META mn_cleared op ('1–3 years ahead of mining'); trucks loaded on the return leg; key_points grade line
findings.issue: The forest label names Darling Range jarrah, but the reference deposit is India East Coast type. mn_cleared says clearing happens 1–3 years ahead of mining; it should be just ahead, to limit bare ground, erosion and dieback spread (1–3 years is the clearing-to-rehab span). Returning trucks still carry a full payload. 'Available' Al₂O₃ is never defined.
findings.correction: Change the label to 'Undisturbed native forest (species vary by region)'. Set mn_cleared op to 'Cleared shortly ahead of mining (weeks to a few months) to keep bare ground to a minimum'. Hide the payload mesh (scale 0.02) on the return half of the loop. Add the key point: 'Available Al₂O₃ = gibbsite alumina extractable in a low-temperature (~145 °C) caustic digest; reactive SiO₂ = kaolinite silica that consumes caustic as DSP.'

findings.where: content params.compressor_flushing_air ('≈ 0.25–0.4 m³/s at ~10 bar'); key_points[4]
findings.issue: The compressor figure covers only top-hammer rigs, but the lesson also teaches DTH, which the basis gives at 20–30 bar. The key point offers 'emulsion/ANFO' with no warning that ANFO fails in wet holes during the monsoon.
findings.correction: P('Top hammer ≈ 10–12 bar; DTH ≈ 20–25 bar; ≈ 0.25–0.4 m³/s', '', 'Class typical'). key_points[4]: 'Holes are dipped, charged with bulk emulsion (always in wet holes) or ANFO (dry holes only) and stemmed under the blast plan.'

area.overall_assessment:
Current status of Area A01 (Mine), 7 models: about 65 % ready for trainees. It is not ready to release yet.

Done and correct:
- Earlier per-model reviews of the haul truck, excavator, dozer and sizing station have been worked into the source files (_eq_m2p_mine.py, content/m2p_mine.py).
- Pass matching is 5–6 passes at about 15 t.
- Fleets are 9 + 2 trucks, 3 excavators and 3 + 1 dozers.
- The canopy-over-cab rule, TKPH and 300 m tyre exclusion, the sizer throughput split, sizer rotation and breaker bar, and the interlock cascades are all in place.
- Haul distance (2–8 km), grades (8 % sustained / 10 % short ramps), road width (≥ 3.5 × truck width), ROM tonnage (6.2–6.4 Mt/yr wet) and rehab rate (60–110 ha/yr) agree across the lessons and with the design basis.
- The fleet arithmetic checks out: about 27 min per cycle, about 1 Mt/yr per truck, and about 4,500 sizer hours.

Blocking items:
1. The built outputs are stale. The overview GLB embeds the pre-fix truck, excavator, dozer and station; the review renders and the station meta JSON predate the fixes. Rebuild with the overview last.
2. Overview safety and realism:
   - Trucks run head-on in a single lane on an unbermed 12 m ramp.
   - Trucks climb a 75 % slope to the tipping deck because the station ramp is cut short and overlaps the ROM pad.
   - Trucks move at about 108 km/h.
   - Caprock and ore are dug as one face, which works against the selective-mining lesson.
   - The drill and loader are not placed in the overview.
3. The drill lesson has no rules about misfires or butts, charged patterns or lightning (critical). Its blast pattern (4 × 4 m) does not match the basis (3.0 × 3.5 m).
4. Wheel loader: the bucket never tips at the dump, its lift is too low to load the truck, the 20 t per pass figure conflicts with 5–6 passes, its safety section is thin, and fleet counts do not match the tags.
5. The wheel stops need to be sized for the loader's larger tyres. Trucks are taught to edge-dump at the ROM pad and waste dumps.
6. The area-level safety content is one line.

Missing items that deserve their own models, in priority order:
1. ROM pad and blending
2. Grade-control RC rig and assays
3. Blasting-cycle lesson with an MMU
4. Water cart and grader
5. Dewatering pump and sediment pond

The design basis also needs updating to match the corrected lessons. Confidence is high on the geometry, animation and consistency findings, which were checked against code and numbers. It is medium on class envelope values, because no web verification was possible.
